# Phantom Secrets

Your agent can call the API. The key stays in a local vault.

Phantom replaces managed secrets in `.env` with `phm_` placeholders. A proxy on `127.0.0.1` adds the vault value only to the auth header of a matched route. Secret values are not printed, logged, or returned to a model.

## 30-second start

Install both binaries from the checksum-verified `v0.8.7` release archive. This is Linux x86_64; take the archive name for macOS, Linux ARM64, or Windows from the [README asset table](README.md#exact-v087-github-assets).

```bash
archive=phantom-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
base=https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom-secrets/releases/download/v0.8.7
curl -fsSL -o "$archive" "$base/$archive"
curl -fsSL -o "$archive.sha256" "$base/$archive.sha256"
sha256sum -c "$archive.sha256"
tar -xzf "$archive"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
install -m 0755 phantom phantom-mcp "$HOME/.local/bin/"
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
phantom init
phantom setup --client claude
phantom status --json
phantom list --json
phantom check --log agent-transcript.jsonl --json
```

On macOS, check the archive with `shasum -a 256 -c "$archive.sha256"`. The Homebrew formula still serves `v0.7.9`, whose `phantom check` has no `--log` or `--json` and which lacks `phantom agent doctor --json` and `--client gemini`. The limits of each package channel are in [docs/distribution-status.md](docs/distribution-status.md).

`phantom status --json`, `phantom list --json`, and `phantom check --log` are value-free. The log scan reports the file, the line, and the credential shape. The same scan is MCP `phantom_check` with `log_path`.

## Ashlr ecosystem

Phantom Secrets is one of the open-source tools from Ashlr (https://ashlr.ai). Together they aim to be an autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory: agents write, test, review, and ship the code, and the human acts as a passive board member. The long-term goal is open-source recursive self-improvement (RSI), where agents improve the tools they build with. Each tool installs and runs on its own:

- Phantom (`phm`, https://phm.dev): the agent workbench. Source: https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom
- Phantom Secrets (`phantom`, this repo): keeps real API-key values out of agent context.
- Locus (`locus`, https://github.com/ashlrai/locus): pins each agent session to one account. This repo ships only an inactive compatibility contract for it (`crates/phantom-locus-contract`).
- Lexicon (`lexicon`, https://lexicon.ashlr.ai): fixes the words dictation gets wrong.
- Ashlr MD (https://md.ashlr.ai): a Markdown app with an MCP server.
- Ashlr Stack (`stack`, https://stack.ashlr.ai): provisions services and stores their keys in Phantom Secrets.
- ashlr-plugin (https://plugin.ashlr.ai/): token-efficiency tools for Claude Code and Codex.

Agents make most changes to this repo through normal pull requests and CI. They follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), use only the value-free commands above, and never need a vault value.

To change this repo, a person or agent follows [Contribute with an agent](CONTRIBUTING.md#contribute-with-an-agent): fork, add this repository as `upstream`, and branch from `upstream/main` (on a fork, use `upstream/main` wherever the commands below say `main`); iterate with `scripts/fast-check.sh main`, which checks only the crates the branch touches; run the full `cargo test`, `cargo fmt --check`, and strict Clippy gate once before opening the pull request, because pull request CI does not run the Rust test suite; add a [`changelog.d/`](changelog.d/README.md) fragment instead of editing `CHANGELOG.md`; before pushing, run the two pre-push checks, `node scripts/changelog-fold.mjs --check` for the fragment format and `git diff main...HEAD | perl .github/tests/secret-shape/scrub.pl --check --allow-fixtures`, the local form of the `Secret-shape scan` that `CI Gate` requires (neither needs a build); and fill in the [pull request template](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) with the exact commands run. `CI Gate` is the only required check, and a passing pull request merges through the merge queue. Fork contributors need no write access or repository secrets.
